nacho.bio: Nacho designs, codes, organizes, and keeps the whole operation from collapsing into digital chaos. From mechanics and UIs to custom Unity tools and project management, he’s the multitasking wizard making sure everything actually ships.

pablo.bio: Pablo shapes the look, style, and essence of every game. The artistic brain behind Los Super Ninis, and a key architect of gameplay ideas. If something is bold, weird, or iconic—he probably invented it.
pablo.kryptonite: Choosing between twenty art styles he created himself

xabi.bio: Xabi speaks fluent shaders. Whether it’s Shader Graph, custom pipelines, or low-level DOTS wizardry, he’s the graphics programmer turning math into magic—and occasionally into mysterious artifacts.

nano.bio: Nano brings worlds to life. He models, textures, rigs, animates, and builds whatever the game needs. If you can see it in 3D, chances are he crafted it with precision (and a bit of suffering).
nano.kryptonite: Hearing the phrase ‘just one more small tweak’

julian.bio: Julián transforms sound into storytelling. He records foley, composes music, designs audio, and wires everything into the engine through FMOD. If it’s satisfying to the ears, he had his hands on it.

symbiosis.desc: A game where you win by doing absolutely nothing. Sleep through levels and avoid responsibilities!

bst.desc: An arcade game about a mouse racing to build a gaming setup.

crop_guardian.desc: An arcade-like game where you fend off hordes of aliens trying to claim your crops.

cafe_chaos.desc: Serve coffee to superheroes who are late for saving the world. Don't spill the latte!

faq1.q: Are your games free to play?
faq1.a: Most of our web games are free! We also have premium versions on Steam with extra hats and zero ads.

faq2.a: Absolutely! We love streamers. If you find a bug live on stream, just pretend it's a feature.

faq3.a: Only if you can beat the dev team in Mario Kart. Send your lap times to our HR department.

faq4.a: We are based in Madrid, Spain! We basically run on tapas and sunshine.
